 Machines are now adding more mobile connections in India than people are
 Jio edges Airtel by a whisker in September, M2M SIMs make up two-thirds of new mobile users, and BSNL’s books look fatter than its network
 Published
 2 days ago on
 October 30, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 NEW DELHI:  India added 6.57 million mobile connections in September. Only 2.22 million of them belonged to humans.
 The rest went into cars, smart meters, payment terminals and fleet trackers. Machine-to-machine (M2M) SIMs jumped from 140.50 million to 144.85 million in a single month, according to the latest numbers from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI). Consumer SIMs inched up from 1,152.93 million to 1,155.15 million. Telcos are still selling plans to people. They are now selling far more to devices.
 Bharti Airtel owns this business. It runs 88.58 million M2M connections, a 61.16 per cent share. Reliance Jio follows with 27.94 million, Vodafone Idea has 23.38 million and BSNL has 4.95 million. When Airtel posts a fat net-addition figure, a good chunk of it does not answer calls.
 The photo finish 
 The two big private players finished almost level. Jio added 2.71 million mobile subscribers and Airtel added 2.69 million, a gap of about 20,500. Jio still leads the market with 511.14 million users and a 39.32 per cent share. Airtel holds 494.29 million and 38.02 per cent. The gap between them is 16.85 million and it barely moved.
 BSNL grew fastest in percentage terms at 0.67 per cent, adding 625,633 users. Vodafone Idea added 550,119, growing at 0.28 per cent, the slowest of the four. Its rural base shrank by about 139,000 even as the overall number rose. MTNL lost 6,628 and keeps fading.
 BSNL’s ghost subscribers 
 The active-user data is less kind to the state-run operator. BSNL reports 94.30 million mobile subscribers. Only 51.36 million were live on its network on the peak day of the month, a ratio of 54.46 per cent. Airtel’s ratio was 98.94 per cent and Jio’s 98.67 per cent. Vodafone Idea sat at 83.85 per cent.
 Across the industry, 1,212.80 million of the 1,300 million mobile connections were active, or 93.29 per cent. The headline number flatters. The active number is the one advertisers and investors should watch.
 Broadband is a two-horse town 
 India now has 1,107.68 million broadband subscribers, up 0.59 per cent from August. Jio holds 541.17 million and Airtel 388.86 million. Together they own nearly 84 per cent of the market. Vodafone Idea has 131 million and BSNL 28.55 million. Atria Convergence (ACT), the largest independent, sits fifth with 2.50 million. The top five control 98.59 per cent.
 Home broadband over the air is where the fresh fight is. 5G fixed wireless access rose to 13.61 million connections. Jio has 9.52 million of those and Airtel 4.09 million. More than half of 5G FWA users, 51.89 per cent, live in rural India, which suggests it is reaching homes where fibre never went. Jio’s unlicensed-band FWA service grew 4.01 per cent to 5.58 million.
 Wired broadband grew more slowly to 48.89 million. Jio leads with 14.92 million, Airtel has 11.55 million and BSNL 4.59 million.
 The landline revival continues 
 Wireline connections rose by 289,462 to 48.74 million. This is fibre-to-the-home riding on a fixed line. Jio added 134,279 and Airtel 124,259. Tata Teleservices put on 45,647. MTNL shed 31,500, the biggest loss by far. Jio now holds 33.06 per cent of wireline subscribers, ahead of Airtel at 25.46 per cent and Tata at 23.07 per cent.
 Restless customers 
 Subscribers are switching more often. Mobile number portability requests rose to 16.77 million in September from 15.83 million in August. Uttar Pradesh (East) led with 2.49 million requests, followed by UP (West) at 1.68 million and Madhya Pradesh at 1.59 million.
 The urban tilt 
 Cities added 5.50 million telephone connections. Villages added 1.73 million. Urban tele-density stands at 155.85 per cent, meaning many city dwellers carry two SIMs or more. Rural tele-density is 61.30 per cent. Delhi tops the chart at 375.65 per cent, helped by the inclusion of Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurgaon and Faridabad. Bihar trails at 64.49 per cent. National tele-density is 95.52 per cent, or 85.41 per cent once M2M SIMs are stripped out.
 India’s total telephone base now stands at 1,367.93 million. The next phase of growth will come from rural homes and connected machines. The handset market in the cities is close to full.
